# `factory/config.py`

[As built](../../README.md) › [Execution environment and infrastructure](../../subsystems/execution-environment-and-infrastructure.md) › `config.py`

As built at `4b8570d19ee1`, read 2026-10-07.

Defines Pydantic configuration models for the factory system, loaded from YAML. Handles routes, roles, provider credentials, and container environments with provider details entirely in configuration, no hardcoding.

2,501 lines, in Execution environment and infrastructure.

## Parts

Too big to be one node, so shown in 10 parts: groups of its functions that call each other more than the rest of the file.

| Part | Lines | Functions | Largest | Calls out · in |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| **Config schema and loading** — Defines the top-level Pydantic models for the factory's configuration -- pipelines, executors, Docker, scheduling, diagnosis, guides, paths and API settings -- and loads/expands a YAML file into them via load_config. It is the backbone the rest of the file reads from and writes back into. | 927 | 15 | `ReworkConfig` | 6 · 4 |
| **Route configuration and defaults** — Defines RouteConfig, the model for a single route, and install_default_route/model_post_init which fill in sensible defaults when a route is only partially specified in YAML. | 291 | 3 | `RouteConfig` | 0 · 1 |
| **Writing staffing assignments** — write_staffing updates which team or role staffs a given route in the YAML file while preserving existing comments, using helpers like team_of, _flow and _set_before to locate and rewrite the right lines. | 217 | 7 | `write_staffing` | 5 · 2 |
| **Writing role and API settings** — write_role and delete_role add, change or remove a role's entry in the config, alongside write_api_settings and write_editor_url for persisting other per-role settings, all via round-tripping YAML that preserves comments and resolving config paths with config_target_path/writable_config_path. | 215 | 12 | `write_role` | 2 · 13 |
| **Checking model independence** — independence_problems checks whether routes or models are improperly shared across families, using landing_family and model_family to determine which family a route or model belongs to. | 112 | 3 | `independence_problems` | 0 · 0 |
| **Suggesting staffing levels** — staffing_suggestions recommends staffing levels for routes, backed by _parse_levels and LevelChoice to interpret level configuration, and write_route_enabled to toggle a route on or off. | 92 | 5 | `staffing_suggestions` | 3 · 1 |
| **Validating route problems** — route_problem_for and its helpers (route, route_for, route_problem) look up a route by key and report whether it is missing, misconfigured or otherwise invalid. | 78 | 5 | `route_problem_for` | 2 · 0 |
| **Managing provider credentials** — write_credential and read_credential persist and retrieve a provider's API key, with api_key_env_name/api_key_source resolving which environment variable or source holds it and credentials_path locating the credentials file. | 56 | 5 | `write_credential` | 0 · 1 |
| **Writing rework limits and executor kind** — write_rework_limits and write_executor_kind update a pipeline's rework limit and executor type in the YAML config, sharing the _rewrite helper to apply the change in place. | 55 | 3 | `write_rework_limits` | 3 · 0 |
| **Writing role prompts** — write_role_prompt and role_prompt set and read the prompt text assigned to a role, using prompt_path to locate the file it is stored in. | 50 | 3 | `write_role_prompt` | 1 · 0 |
